# M4: Mount the two four-screw terminal strips on the chassis rear

> *Mount the two four screw terminal strips on the chassis rear from the outside. Fasten with 4/40 hardware.* — manual page 4

## What you're doing physically

The kit includes two **4-screw terminal strips** (also called "barrier strips") — these are the speaker output terminals on the back of the amp. One per channel (left and right). Each has four threaded studs that accept bare speaker wire under the screw heads.

Mount each strip on the rear panel from OUTSIDE the chassis, with the threaded studs sticking outward (so speaker wires connect from outside). Two #4-40 screws hold each strip, with kep nuts on the inside.

## Why 4-screw strips (not 2)

Each strip provides four taps corresponding to:

| Strip lug | Label | Connects to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16 Ω | YELLOW lead from A-470 secondary |
| 2 | 8 Ω | ORANGE lead from A-470 secondary |
| 3 | 4 Ω | BROWN lead from A-470 secondary |
| 4 | C (common) | BLACK lead from A-470 secondary + ground link |

Different speakers have different impedance ratings (4Ω, 8Ω, or 16Ω). The 4-screw strip exposes all three taps so you can choose which tap matches your speaker. You always use the "C" common terminal plus one of the impedance taps.

For most modern speakers, you'll use the **8Ω tap (lug 2) and C (lug 4)**.

## Why both strips look identical

The two strips are interchangeable — one channel's strip is mechanically identical to the other's. The labels typically distinguish left from right based on which side of the chassis they're mounted on (looking at the back of the amp: left speaker on the LEFT, right on the RIGHT, matching the convention from inside the amp).
